 Hon'Ble Anish Kumar Gupta, J.

1 .  Second supplementary affidavit filed by learned counsel for the applicants, today in the Court,
which is taken on record.
The certified copy of the compromise verification has also been annexed as Annexure No. SA-1 to the second supplementary affidavit.

2. Heard Sri Anish Kumar Sihna, Advocate, holding brief of Sri Arvind Srivastava III, learned counsel for the applicants and Sri Rajesh Kumar Mishra, learned counsel for the opposite party no.
2 and Sri Pankaj Srivastava, learned A.G.A. for the State.
3.

The applicant has invoked the inherent jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C. for quashing of the entire proceedings of Criminal Case No. 822 of 2023 (State Vs. Vimal Kumar and others), arising out of Case Crime No. 113/2023, under Sections 498A, 323, 504 & 354B of I.P.C. &
3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station- Milak, District- Rampur, pending before Civil Judge (Junior Division/Fast Track Court/Crime Against Women), Rampur.
4.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for applicants submits that the instant case is arising out of the matrimonial dispute between the applicant no.1 and the opposite party no.2, due to which F.I.R was filed on 01.06.2023 by the opposite party no. 2. and all the applicants have been implicated in the instant case.

The matter was investigated and the Charge-sheet was filed against the applicants, thereafter cognizance was taken by the learned trial court vide order dated 11.10.2023 against the applicants no. 2 & 4 respectively.

During the pendency of the instant case the applicant no. 1 and the opposite party no. 2 have entered into amicable settlement on their own freewill and a compromise between the parties was executed on 07.01.2025.

A certified copy of the compromise-deed dated 07.01.2025 has been annexed as Annexure No. SA No. 1 to the supplementary affidavit filed on 01.07.2025.
5.

In view of the aforesaid facts, this Court initially vide order dated 08.08.2025 has directed the parties to appear before the trial court concerned for verification of the compromise executed between them.
Thus, in terms of the aforesaid, a report dated 16.09.2025 has been received from the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 2, Rampur.

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 2, Rampur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: According to which, the parties have appeared before the trial court on 15.09.2025 and in the presence of the parties, the said compromise has been duly verified by the trial court.
Copy of the order compromise verification order has been produced along with the report as well as the copy of compromise.
It is a matrimonial dispute between the applicant no. 1 and opposite party no. 2, which has been duly settled between them amicably.
Thus, learned counsel for the applicants seeks quashing of the entire proceedings of the instant case against the applicants herein.

6. Learned counsel for opposite party no. 2 do not dispute the aforesaid facts and admits the execution of compromise and its verification as well, thus he supports the prayer for quashing of the entire proceedings against the applicants in the instant case in view of the compromise arrived at between the parties.

sentences.text: Learned AGA, looking at the facts and circumstances of the case and its settlement and verification of the compromise, does not oppose the prayer for quashing of the criminal proceedings of the instant case against the applicants herein.
8. Having heard the submissions so made by learned counsel for the parties, this Court has carefully gone through the record of the case.
From the record of the case, it is apparent that it is a matrimonial discord between the parties, due to which the opposite party no.2 has lodged the instant case against the applicants herein.

As per the order passed by this Court on 08.08.2025, the parties have appeared before the trial court for verification of compromise, which has been accordingly verified by the trial court and a report in this regard has been submitted.

9. Since, it was a matrimonial dispute between the parties, which has been amicably settled and the compromise executed has been verified by the trial court, therefore, in the considered opinion of this Court, and no fruitful purpose will be served by keeping the criminal proceeding pending against the applicants herein and due to the aforesaid compromise there are very remote and bleak chances of the conviction of the applicants.
Further, with the aforesaid settlement of matrimonial dispute, peace will prevail not only in the families of the parties but in society at large.

Thus, in the light of the judgment of the Apex Court in Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and Another : (2012) 10 SCC 303; Prabatbhai Aahir Alias Prabatbhai Bhimsinghbhai Karmur and others vs. State of Gujarat and Another : (2017) 9 SCC 641; Narinder Singh & Ors. vs. State of Punjab : (2014) 6 SCC 466 and B.S.Joshi and Other vs. State of Haryana and Another : (2003) 4 SCC 67, the instant application is allowed and the entire proceedings in Criminal Case No. 822 of 2023 (State Vs. Vimal Kumar and others), arising out of Case Crime No. 113/2023, under Sections 498A, 323, 504 & 354B of I.P.C. &
3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station- Milak, District- Rampur, pending before Civil Judge (Junior Division/Fast Track Court/Crime Against Women), Rampur, are hereby quashed.
(Anish Kumar Gupta,J.) November 6, 2025 Vibha Singh
